newsitem.title: UK: IBCA may up BB plus long-term rating of Uruguay.
newsitem.headline: IBCA may up BB plus long-term rating of Uruguay.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Tuesday it had placed the BB plus long-term foreign currency rating of the Oriental Republic of Uruguay on RatingWatch with positive implications.
"The rating was first assigned by the agency in January 1995," IBCA said in a statement.

The agency said that in its view, Uruguay's previous electoral system, by encouraging factionalism and virtually guaranteeing weak minority governments, had been an obstacle to the implementation of structural reforms.

"Even so, the constitutional reform adds to a string of achievements since 1990," it said. "Paramount among these has been the commitment to reforming the public finances, including long-overdue reform of the social security system."
"In force since April 1996, a partially privatised pension system has been a success, having attracted 300,000 affiliates, almost 10 percent of the total population," IBCA said.
"Meanwhile, the annual inflation rate has halved to 24 per cent over the the past two years."
